C1810.title: Raven II Surgical Robot Teleoperation Hijacking Research
C1810.summary: In May 2015, a University of Washington team performed the first experimental security attacks on the Raven II open-source remote surgical robot, revealing its teleoperation channel could be hijacked. Researchers could trigger emergency stops, perform man-in-the-middle attacks to tamper with control commands, and inject malicious actions, proving the encryption and authentication gaps in remote surgical robots. MIT Tech Review reported this as the first surgical-robot teleoperation hijacking study, driving medical-robot communication-security standards.
